items.title: Section: Eleven Remedies Matched to Twelve Failings, and the Ground of Non-Meditative-Equipoise Closes

items.zh: 依止初不定地，為安住心，應正取相。謂青瘀相、或膿爛相，廣說如前。依止第二不定地故，為得作意，應勤修習。依止第三不定地故，為得根本，應勤修習。依止第四現在前故，最初應正安住其念，為無亂故，略攝其心；由正知故，速疾攝受。依止第五現在前故，應當思惟淨妙之相，又應善達沈沒之相。依止第六現在前故，於師教授，能不忘失。應當安住猛利護念如理方便。應當無間、殷重修習。依止第七現在前故，應於微劣所得定中，不生喜足。依止第八現在前故，於諸雜染應觀過失；設生愛味，所有雜染尋即除遣，不應戀著。依止第九現在前故，於三摩地應無間修。又應善巧通達其相。依止第十現在前故，應當猛利修諦善巧。依第十一現在前故，為令不退，應不放逸。依第十二現在前故，即為彼事，應修遠離如理作意，應隨順前修習無間、殷重方便。於此地中餘決擇文，更不復現。如是已說非三摩呬多地決擇。有心地決擇，我今當說。
items.en: When the twelfth non-concentrated condition, falling back, is present, for this very matter, one should cultivate correct reflection on release from it, and should follow the earlier practice, uninterrupted and earnest. The remaining decisive-discernment texts on this ground will not appear again. The decisive discernment of the Ground possessing mind, within the chapter of decisive discernment. Thus I have already explained the decisive discernment of the Ground of Non-Meditative-Equipoise. I shall now explain the decisive discernment of the Ground possessing mind.

items.title: Section: A Fifth Ground Opens — Distinguishing Mind Present from Mind Absent

items.zh: 當知諸心差別而轉，略由五相。一、由世俗道理建立故；二、由勝義道理建立故；三、由所依能依建立故；四、由俱有建立故；五、由染淨建立故。
items.en: One should know that the distinct functioning of every mind can, briefly, be established through five aspects: through conventional truth; through ultimate truth; through what is depended upon and what depends; through what co-exists together; and through defilement and purity.

items.zh: 云何世俗道理建立？謂依世俗道理建立諸心差別轉義，當知如前意地已說。勝義道理建立差別，我今當說。云何名為勝義道理建立差別？

items.title: Section: The Ālaya as Depended-Upon, the Six Active Consciousnesses as Depending

items.zh: 謂略有二識。一者、阿賴耶識，二者、轉識。阿賴耶識是所依，轉識是能依。此復七種、所謂眼識乃至意識。譬如水浪依止暴流，或如影像依止明鏡。如是名依勝義道理，建立所依能依差別。
items.en: There are, briefly, two kinds of consciousness: the ālaya-consciousness, and the transforming consciousnesses. The ālaya-consciousness is what is depended upon; the transforming consciousnesses are what depends upon it, these being six in number, from eye consciousness through mind consciousness. It is like waves depending on a torrent, or a reflection depending on a bright mirror. This is called establishing the distinction between what is depended upon and what depends, through ultimate truth.

items.title: Section: Mind, Mentation, and Consciousness — Three Names for Eight Working Together

items.zh: 復次，此中諸識，皆名心、意、識。若就最勝，阿賴耶識名心。何以故？由此識能集聚一切法種子故，於一切時緣執受境，緣不可知一類器境。末那名意，於一切時執我我所及我慢等，思量為性。餘識名識，謂於境界了別為相。如是三種，有心位中心、意、意識，於一切時俱有而轉。若眼識等轉識不起。彼若起時，應知彼增俱有而轉。如是或時四識俱轉，乃至或時八識俱轉。又一意識，於一時間分別一境，或二或多、自境他境，故說意識不可思議。問：若彼末那，於一切時思量為性，相續而轉。如世尊說出世末那，云何建立？
items.en: Furthermore, all these consciousnesses are called mind, mentation, and consciousness. In terms of what excels most, the ālaya-consciousness is called mind. Manas is called mentation, deliberating at all times upon self, what belongs to self, and pride of self as its own nature. The remaining consciousnesses are called consciousness, discerning their objects being their character. These three, mind, mentation, and mental consciousness, remain present together at all times throughout a mind-possessing state. Question: if manas deliberates at all times as its own nature, continuing without break, how can the World-Honoured One's own teaching of a transcendent manas be established?

items.title: Section: A Name Need Not Match Its Own Meaning, and the Ālaya's Own Untroubled Feeling

items.zh: 答：名假施設，不必如義。又對治彼，遠離顛倒正思量故。即此末那任持意識，令分別轉。是故說為意識所依。又諸轉識，或於一時一切唯與樂受相應俱有而轉，或於一時亦有苦受，或於一時亦有不苦不樂等受相應俱轉。阿賴耶識相應受，於一切時唯是不苦不樂，唯是異熟生。此於一切識流轉時，或樂俱行、或苦俱行、或非苦樂俱行位中，恒相續流，乃至命終無有斷絕。
items.en: Answer: names are conventionally designated and need not match their meaning. It also counters that defiled manas, departing from distortion through correct deliberation. This very manas sustains mental consciousness, allowing it to discriminate, and so is called its support. The transforming consciousnesses may at one time all be associated with pleasant feeling, at another with painful feeling, at another with neither painful nor pleasant feeling. The feeling associated with the ālaya-consciousness is, at all times, only neither painful nor pleasant, being solely the ripening of past karma. Throughout the flow of every consciousness, whether accompanied by pleasure, by pain, or by neither, it continues unbroken until life itself ends.

items.zh: 所餘三受，當知思惟之所引發，非是俱生，時時作意引發現前。彼俱生受極微細故，難可分別。如是等類，當知是名勝義道理，建立諸識俱有差別。

blocks.text: A new stage: the Stage With Mind and Without Mind. The treatise uses it to set out the eight consciousnesses together.
Master Cháng Bǎi: to treat falling from absorption, practise right attention that leaves the causes of the loss, and follow the method by which concentration was first won.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the ālaya is what is depended on; the transforming consciousnesses depend on it. (Untranslated, 0651b11: by conventional truth, the distinctions of mind were explained in the Stage of Mind; now, by ultimate truth.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: waves exist only because of the torrent. The ālaya holds the seeds of the transforming consciousnesses.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "mind" (citta) is the eighth; "mentation" (manas), which excels in deliberation, the seventh; "consciousness" (vijñāna), which discerns, the sixth.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is provisional. Defiled manas deliberates on a self; the purified manas rightly deliberates on no-self. The sixth consciousness relies on manas as its support. The ālaya's feeling is born of ripening, innate, and always neutral. (Untranslated, 0651c10: the other feelings arise from attention, not innately; the innate one is so subtle it is hard to discern.)
"A name need not match its meaning." Even "manas", the self-grasping mind, keeps its name after it is purified.

quiz.q: This is rendered "Relying on the twelfth present state." Why can it not be understood?
options: it means when the twelfth non-concentrated condition, falling back, is present, and the prior eleven are missing
it can be: it is the twelfth present moment of thought, as the lecture explains
it should be "the twelfth absorption"
it should be "the twelfth precept"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on the twelfth non-concentrated ground being present, which is the one through falling back. The remedies for the other eleven are missing, so a reader of the English has no way to know what "twelfth" refers to.

quiz.q: How is the twelfth, falling back, to be remedied, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: cultivate right attention leaving the causes of loss, and follow the earlier method, uninterrupted and earnest
give up that concentration for another, since a lost one cannot be practised
ask a teacher for blessing
first be reborn in heaven and then practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to treat falling from absorption, practice right attention that leaves the causes of the loss, and follow the method by which concentration was first gained, uninterrupted and earnest, again and again. The earlier method is reused.

quiz.q: By which five aspects does the treatise establish the distinct functioning of mind?
options: form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, the usual division of mind
eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body
wholesome, unwholesome, neutral, with outflow, undefiled
conventional truth, ultimate truth, what depends and is depended upon, co-existence, and defilement and purity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ālaya is what is depended on and the transforming consciousnesses what depend on it; defilement and purity concern the coexisting consciousnesses. The English omits the explanations of the first two, so only the five names are tested.

quiz.q: What similes does the treatise use for depending and depended upon?
options: waves depending on a torrent, and a reflection depending on a bright mirror
a sprout depending on a seed, and fruit on a flower, the usual seed simile, as here
a flame on oil, a wheel on an axle
a pot on a potter, gold work on a goldsmith
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: waves are what depend and the torrent is what is depended on, since waves exist only because of the torrent. The bright mirror stands for the ālaya, and his link to the great mirror wisdom is the lecture's own addition.

quiz.q: Why is the ālaya-consciousness what the transforming consciousnesses depend on?
options: it arises first in time and stops when they arise
the ālaya is a physical faculty on which they rest
the ālaya is an outer object they take
the ālaya stores their seeds, and only when seeds manifest can they function
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ālaya holds the seeds of the transforming consciousnesses, and only when those seeds manifest can they function. He adds that the conventional account is by six consciousnesses, and the ultimate by eight.

quiz.q: In terms of what excels most, what are mind, mentation, and consciousness?
options: manas is mind, the ālaya mentation, and the remainder consciousness
mental consciousness is mind, manas consciousness, the ālaya mentation
the ālaya is called mind, manas mentation, and the remaining ones consciousness
all three are the sixth consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: deliberation is called mentation, and manas excels in deliberation among the consciousnesses; discerning is called consciousness, and the six excel in that. Generally all eight may bear all three names, as the treatise said first.

quiz.q: This is rendered "mind, mentation, and consciousness, remain present together at all times." Why does it clash with what follows?
options: no clash: all eight are always present, the five included, as the lecture agrees
有心位 should be "waking state"
the third is 意識, the sixth alone, while the same English word implies all six always present
俱有 should be "separately"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in a state with mind, the three are the eighth, seventh, and sixth consciousnesses. Earlier in the section the English word "consciousness" means all six, so reused here it seems to say the five senses are constantly active.

quiz.q: If manas deliberates as its nature, how is the transcendent manas established?
options: the name is designated and need not match; also it counters that, with correct deliberation free of distortion
it is a wholly separate consciousness, only the name being shared
the Buddha never taught it
manas turns into the ālaya when transcendent
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is provisional, and one need not read the transcendent manas by the literal name. Defiled manas deliberates on self, and pure manas deliberates on no-self. So two answers are given, one about names and one about deliberation.

quiz.q: This is rendered "counters that very deliberation ... through correct contemplation." What is the problem?
options: it counters the stain, not deliberation; correct 思量 is still 思量, a link the English breaks
none: transcendent manas ends deliberation entirely, as the lecture says
顛倒 should be "wrong view"
it should be "correct knowing"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it counters the stain of manas, leaving distorted self-view and the rest, and rightly deliberates on no-self. Because this remains deliberation, it can still bear the name manas, which is the point the English loses.

quiz.q: Why is manas called the support of mental consciousness, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: manas stores its seeds, doing the ālaya's work
it is manas's ripened result
it needs manas to see forms
the sixth consciousness relies on manas as its mental faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the sixth consciousness relies on manas as its mental faculty, so manas is called its support. The treatise says manas sustains mental consciousness and lets it discriminate. Storing seeds belongs to the ālaya, not to manas.

quiz.q: What feeling is associated with the ālaya-consciousness?
options: it varies with the transforming consciousnesses, now pleasant and now painful, never fixed
only pleasant feeling
at all times only neither painful nor pleasant, solely the ripening of past karma
only painful feeling
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is feeling born of the ripening of karma, innate, called ripened feeling. Transforming consciousnesses can have any of the three feelings at different times, while the ālaya has only neutral feeling, unbroken.

quiz.q: When transforming consciousnesses have pleasant or painful feeling, what of the ālaya's neutral feeling?
options: it stops for the moment, two feelings being impossible at once
it turns into pleasant feeling
it turns into painful feeling
it goes on arising, continuing constantly until life's end
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the neutral feeling of the ālaya continues arising, ever flowing on. The treatise says this holds whether pleasure, pain, or neither accompanies the others. The opposition of feelings in §35 applies only among transforming consciousnesses.
